wheel.offset: +37 mm on Rubicon 17x7.5 (≈5.7 in backspacing); about +44 mm on Sport/Sahara

max_tire.size: 33 in; 35 in on gas Rubicon with bump-stop spacers
max_tire.note: A 35 clears a gas Rubicon at ride height but rubs the inner fenders under compression; bump stops fix it at the cost of about 2 in of up-travel. The Rubicon 4xe sits about 2 in lower, so bump stops are a must.
Jeep's factory package from 2021 for the four-door Rubicon and 392: 1.5 in lift, 4.56 gears and 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels.
What Sport and Sahara (and the 4xe) need for 35s, together with bump stops and about 4.5–5.0 in backspacing.

items.title: Front track bar bracket welds (the 'frame weld' recall)
items.summary: Track bar brackets may be improperly welded and separate from the frame, reducing steering; dealers inspect and repair the welds (recall UA5, 18,055 vehicles).

items.title: Intermediate steering shaft weld
items.summary: The shaft may not have been properly welded and can split, so the wheel loses centre (recall U48).

items.title: Rear underbody ladder rail corrosion
items.summary: The rail can corrode, weakening the rear floor and loosening the left rear seat mount; dealers apply rust protection (recall U27, 106 vehicles).

items.title: Steering column stub shaft
items.summary: Improperly machined stub shafts can break and detach the steering wheel (recall V29).

items.title: Manual-transmission clutch pressure plate
items.summary: Pressure plate may overheat and fracture (recall W12).

items.title: Clutch overheating software
items.summary: Software reduces engine torque when the clutch gets too hot; FCA ordered a stop-sale in February 2021.

items.title: Clutch assembly replacement
items.summary: Dealers replace the clutch assembly and update software (recall 19A); 24V-572 re-fixes some 2021 trucks.

items.title: Left lower control arm bracket weld
items.summary: Bracket and weld may be mispositioned (recall W01, 3,005 vehicles).

items.title: Frame stud can puncture fuel tank
items.summary: In a crash a frame stud may puncture the tank (recall 28A).

items.title: Instrument cluster short
items.summary: The cluster can short internally and fail (recall 30B).

items.title: Electric-hydraulic power steering pump wiring fire
items.summary: Pump wiring can overheat and start a fire even when parked; owners told to park outside until repaired (1,076,999 vehicles across Wrangler and Gladiator).

items.title: 3.0 EcoDiesel high-pressure fuel pump
items.summary: The HPFP may fail and stall the engine (recall Z96).

items.title: 3.0 EcoDiesel high-pressure fuel pump (expansion)
items.summary: Same pump failure on later diesels (recall 01A).

items.title: 4xe high-voltage battery fire (first campaign)
items.summary: Battery may fail internally and catch fire; owners told not to charge and to park outside until repaired (32,125 vehicles).

items.title: 4xe high-voltage battery fire (expanded)
items.summary: Same fire risk on a wider population; replaced by 25V-741, so trucks fixed under it need the new remedy.

items.title: 4xe high-voltage battery fire (current remedy)
items.summary: Software update and battery replacement as needed; park outside and don't charge until done (320,068 vehicles incl. Grand Cherokee 4xe).

items.title: 4xe HV battery 200-amp fuse fasteners
items.summary: Wrong fasteners on the 200-amp fuse can overheat and cut drive power; reissued as 23V-303.

items.title: 4xe engine shutdown on lost communication
items.summary: A communication loss can shut the engine down.

items.title: 4xe over-the-air update loss of drive
items.summary: A software error in an OTA update can cause loss of drive power (recall A7C).

items.title: 4xe engine debris
items.summary: Debris inside the engine can cause failure or an engine-bay fire (recall 78C).

items.title: Rear door latch (four-door)
items.summary: Right rear door latch may be mislocated and not latch (recall UB6).

tsbs.title: Death wobble: steering damper replacement
tsbs.summary: About 192,000 2018–2019 JLs get a new front steering damper for a sustained steering-wheel shimmy after bumps, especially above 55 mph and below 40°F. It's a customer satisfaction notification, not a safety recall.

tsbs.title: Steering-wheel shimmy after road irregularities
tsbs.summary: November 2019 bulletin for 2018–2020 JL (and 2020 Gladiator) that points technicians to a diagnosis and repair video for the steering linkage and damper.

timeline.change: JL launch (four-door production from November 2017, two-door from early 2018): 3.6 Pentastar with a 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto, plus a 2.0 turbo with eTorque (auto only). Early trucks need the track-bar weld, steering-shaft and V41 damper fixes.
3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp) arrives, four-door only; later subject to high-pressure fuel pump recalls

Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid (375 hp, 21-mile EV range) and Rubicon 392 (6.4 Hemi, 470 hp), both four-door only. Xtreme Recon package (35s, 4.56 gears, 1.5 in lift) for the four-door Rubicon and 392; 4.88 axles optional on Rubicon.
Facelift: new grille (except Sport/Sport S), standard 12-inch Uconnect 5, new Rubicon X trim. Xtreme 35 package reaches the two-door. EcoDiesel dropped. Rubicon 392 'Final Edition'.
Rubicon 392 continues, still badged 'Final Edition'; last US model year for the 4xe
Moab 392 tops the range (four-door only); reworked door hinges for easier removal; 3.6 still offered with the manual; 4xe dropped as Stellantis phases out plug-in hybrids

identify.intro: The four-door JL comes with five powertrains, and the 4xe, 392 and EcoDiesel were four-door only. Check what's under the hood before you look at anything else.

items.head: Real Rubicon
items.body: Dana 44s front and rear with Tru-Lok electronic lockers, Rock-Trac with 4:1 low range, and an electronic sway-bar disconnect. Sport and Sahara have a Dana 30 front, a Dana 35 rear (optional Trac-Lok) and Command-Trac with 2.72:1.

items.head: 4xe
items.body: Plug-in hybrid with a 2.0 turbo, 17 kWh battery, 375 hp and 470 lb-ft; it has a charge port and a smaller 17.2-gal tank. Check that the battery-fire recall (25V-741) has been done.

items.head: Rubicon 392
items.body: 6.4 Hemi with 470 hp and 470 lb-ft, four-door only, on LT315/70R17s from the factory. Sold 2021–2025 as the Rubicon 392 ('Final Edition' in 2024–25), then as the Moab 392 for 2026.

items.head: EcoDiesel
items.body: 3.0 VM Motori turbodiesel V6 (260 hp), four-door only, 2020–2023. Check the high-pressure fuel pump recalls (22V-767 and 23V-263) have been completed.

items.head: Xtreme Recon
items.body: Factory LT315/70R17 BFGoodrich KO2s on 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels, 4.56 gears and a 1.5 in lift, offered from 2021 on the four-door Rubicon and 392.

items.head: Selec-Trac
items.body: The optional full-time MP3022 Selec-Trac transfer case (2.72:1 low) is a Sahara option; Rubicons use Rock-Trac (4:1).

capability.note: Sport to Rubicon; 12.9 in (328 mm) with the Xtreme Recon package
Rubicon; 47.4° / 40.4° / 26.7° with the Xtreme Recon package
31.5 in on Rubicon 4xe; 33.6 in with the Xtreme Recon package
4xe: EPA 49 MPGe / 20 mpg combined, 21-mile electric range

values.intro: Ordinary four-door JLs have sunk to used-SUV money, but the 392 holds its value well. A late, low-mile Rubicon 392 still brings most of its sticker.
values.note: Based on about 35 four-door JL and 33 Rubicon 392 sales on Bring a Trailer in 2025–26. The 392 median was about $65.5k, and EcoDiesel Rubicons brought $40k–43k.
